plan: dispatch://INFRA-629/artifact/plan-md (version 1). Summary: changie v1.26.0, one .changie.yaml per package (seven), fragments packages/<pkg>/.changes/unreleased/<ISSUE KEY>-<slug>.yaml (kind Added|Changed|Removed|Fixed, body). A new serialized workflow .github/workflows/changelog-fold.yaml (workflow_run of Release Packages and Release Envoy Listener on main, daily schedule, workflow_dispatch; concurrency group changelog-fold) folds every package from main's tip: fold_build (no credential; install-changie; release-push.sh fold-plan + fold-notes; tripwire) and fold_publish (deploy key only in the push-fold step; release-push.sh fold recomputes the plan with git and checks the notes; push-fold checks the commit before every push). Versioned packages (envoy-plugin, pi-envoy, pi-legion, envoy) fold each fragment under the lowest-version release tag containing the commit that added it; claude-envoy, contracts, envoy-client fold under main@<12 hex>. Heading '## [<label>] - <YYYY-MM-DD>'. release-push.sh's existing subcommands, release.yaml and release-envoy-listener.yaml do not change. The seven '## [Unreleased]' headings become '## Before changelog fragments' (departure 2, droppable). Files in order, tests, and the six acceptance proofs are in plan.md.

implement: legion-worker: the implementer's PR body, proofs at the head and simplify pass (references/pr-body.md), the push and identity checks (references/default-branch-check.md), and references/cleanup-deletion.md for deleting .changelog/516.md
ce-simplify-code: the one simplify pass over release-push.sh's new subcommands and the new workflow after the proofs
asd-ste100: the new AGENTS.md convention bullet, the four README sentences and the solution-doc edits are explanatory prose agents read
test: legion-worker: the tester's proof objects (references/pr-body.md#what-a-proof-is) for the six acceptance criteria, each with a negative control, and references/tools.md to install changie v1.26.0 under $TMPDIR from the pinned tarball
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md and references/review-threads.md for the review of the head by SHA, with the build/publish credential boundary (root AGENTS.md 'Release jobs keep credentials away from dependency code') as the security focus of the new workflow and push-fold

findings.finding: Folding inside the release jobs breaks pushed_tag's re-run detection (release-push.sh:245-246, release-push.test.sh:541-550), empties the fold set on a re-run, and strands fragments for good when a fold's push to main is lost.
findings.answer: The fold leaves the release jobs: a separate serialized workflow computes the fold from main's tip and the tags after each release, so a lost push is redone by the next run and the bump path (tag, tagged, version, push-main) does not change. Recorded as departure 1.

findings.finding: Overlapping runs fold the same fragments twice (the listener's release_build runs outside its concurrency group; changelog-fold.yaml had no group).
findings.answer: changelog-fold.yaml has a workflow-level concurrency group with cancel-in-progress false, pinned by a new rule 7 in check-release-credentials.sh; push-fold refuses when a planned fragment was deleted or edited on main since the build.

findings.finding: Bytes chosen by the build job (notes, fragment list) would land on main.
findings.answer: The publish job recomputes the plan with git and never takes a list from the build job; notes must be exactly one regular file per planned (package, label), non-empty, no NUL, no line starting '## '; push-fold checks the commit is exactly the planned insertions and deletions. The fold build job runs no dependency code but the checksum-pinned changie.

findings.finding: push-main needs more than one new rule: one commit per package-dir, no manifest for the listener, superseded-per-part rewrites, modify/delete conflicts, a date-independent landed check.
findings.answer: push-main is unchanged; a new push-fold checks one fold commit across the seven packages, needs no manifest, exits 0 when main holds the commit, aborts and fails on any rebase conflict, and headings take the tag's (or tip's) commit date in UTC so a re-run writes the same bytes.

findings.finding: Unmeasured changie behaviour: non-semver label, zero fragments, missing unreleased dir, partial batch, multi-line body rendering, empty versionFormat.
findings.answer: The heading is written by fold, so changie is always called as 'changie batch 0.0.0' with versionFormat '' (measured: output is the kind sections after blank lines, which fold trims); fold-notes calls changie only for a non-empty group, in a temporary directory holding only that group's fragments; changelog-fold.test.sh pins multi-line rendering and kind order with the real binary.

findings.finding: Fold commits need [skip ci] and a fixed message, or they start the listener and image workflows and release-bump.sh may read fragment text from the body.
findings.answer: Fixed message 'chore: fold changelog fragments [skip ci]', no body; asserted in release-push.test.sh.

findings.finding: Acceptance 2 tests: the test job lists each script as its own step; 'given fragments' needs changie; the refusals must be listed.
findings.answer: pr-and-main.yaml's test job gains install-changie and a step for the new changelog-fold.test.sh, which refuses to pass without changie v1.26.0; plan.md lists every accept and refuse case of fold and push-fold.

findings.finding: check-release-credentials.sh needs WORKFLOWS, header, changie in DEPENDENCY_COMMANDS, test fixture and count, a concurrency rule; listener header and packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:4167 would go stale.
findings.answer: All listed in the plan; the listener workflow and packages/envoy/AGENTS.md are untouched in this design, so they stay true and the overlap with INFRA-631 disappears.

findings.finding: Renaming '## [Unreleased]' is a product choice; the conflict measurement covered one insertion shape; an old-style entry after the rename merges silently into the frozen section.
findings.answer: Recorded as departure 2 for the architect, droppable without touching anything else; acceptance 5 measures conflicts against every open pull request touching a CHANGELOG.md; the instruction tells open pull requests to move their entry, and review catches one that did not.

findings.finding: Fragment naming rule ambiguous (several per PR, no Dispatch key, second PR on one issue); workers have no changie; .changelog/516.md is a second convention.
findings.answer: Name '<ISSUE KEY or branch name>-<slug>.yaml', a slug per fragment; the instruction gives the hand-written YAML and the 'go run github.com/miniscruff/changie@v1.26.0 new' form (measured to work in the pod); .changelog/516.md is deleted.

findings.finding: Acceptance 4 can be met by one package, proving one path of three.
findings.answer: The production check names two looks: a fold run after a versioned release with fragments, and a fold of a claude-envoy, contracts or envoy-client fragment under main@; pending until both.

findings.finding: Unsupported spec claims: claude-envoy CHANGELOG.md:207,210 and suggestions_test.go:488-497 do not point into [Unreleased]; check-plugin-names lists changelogs by exact path, so fragments are not covered; changie's default kinds.
findings.answer: The two pointer sites are read and left unchanged with reasons in plan.md; check-plugin-names.sh gains the four .changes/ directory prefixes with their reason; kinds are set explicitly (Added, Changed, Removed, Fixed).

specDepartures.spec: Outcome: 'the release job writes the new entries into it under the released version when it cuts that release'; Acceptance 2: 'push-main's checks accept exactly that commit and still refuse anything else'; Acceptance 4: 'the first release of a package after the merge, run by the real workflow on main, folds that package's fragments'.
specDepartures.plan: A new serialized workflow, changelog-fold.yaml, started by each release workflow's completion (and daily), writes each entry under the version of the release that first shipped it, in a commit on main pushed by a new release-push.sh push-fold; its checks, not push-main's, are what the tests prove. push-main, the bump commit, release.yaml and release-envoy-listener.yaml do not change. The production check names the fold run a release starts.
specDepartures.evidence: Folding inside the release job needs changes to pushed_tag's re-run detection (release-push.sh:245-246, pinned by release-push.test.sh:541-550), push-main's superseded exit that drops the whole commit (:584-597) and its rebase repair (:601-627); a fold whose push is lost is then never redone, and the listener's release_build runs outside its concurrency group, so two runs can fold the same fragments. A fold computed from main's tip in a serialized workflow is idempotent and leaves the release path untouched.

summary: Outcome: 'the release job writes the new entries…' becomes 'a fold job, run after each release, writes the new entries into it under the released version'
acceptance: 4: 'the first release … folds' becomes 'the fold run that the first release's completion starts folds'

specDepartures.spec: Outcome: 'Each package's CHANGELOG.md keeps all of its existing text'.
specDepartures.plan: Every entry and line stays, except that each '## [Unreleased]' heading becomes '## Before changelog fragments', so a released section above it does not call older, released entries unreleased. Droppable on the architect's word with nothing else changing.
specDepartures.evidence: Release sections are inserted above that heading; most entries under it shipped (48 legion-envoy releases). Measured: the rename and an old-style insertion after the first '### ' line merge clean (git merge-tree, pi-legion, envoy, claude-envoy).

summary: Outcome: 'keeps all of its existing text' becomes 'keeps all of its entries; its [Unreleased] heading is renamed'

specDepartures.spec: Scope: 'Decide in the plan how the listener (tag only) and the three packages with no release of their own get their fragments folded'.
specDepartures.plan: The listener's fragments fold under the legion-envoy-v release that first carried them; claude-envoy, contracts and envoy-client fold at each fold run under '## [main@<12 hex>] - <date>', a heading that is not a version.
specDepartures.evidence: contracts 0.10.0, envoy-client 0.1.0 and claude-envoy 1.0.0 have static versions, no tag and no release workflow; Claude Code installs claude-envoy from main's tree.
